coromandel-6.name: Thames
coromandel-6.bio: An old gold-mining town and the largest on the peninsula, the gateway to the Kauaeranga Valley.
notes: Town spot; no ticketUrl (no single steward).

coromandel-7.name: Whitianga
coromandel-7.bio: A Mercury Bay harbour town where cruising boats leave for the bay's coves and Te Whanganui-A-Hei Marine Reserve.

coromandel-8.name: Kauaeranga Valley
coromandel-8.bio: A Coromandel Forest Park valley with riverside campsites, kauri logging displays and the track to the Pinnacles.

coromandel-9.name: Pinnacles Track
coromandel-9.bio: A DOC track of about 6 km each way from the Kauaeranga road end to Pinnacles Hut and the 759 m summit lookout.
notes: Coordinates are the OSM Webb Creek first node near the road end (DOC gives none). Visit time 6-8 from DOC 6-7.5 hr return. Hut bunks are separate.

coromandel-10.name: Pauanui
coromandel-10.bio: A town at the mouth of the Tairua River, opposite Tairua, for swimming, surfing, kayaking and fishing.
notes: Single counted source; marginal draw.

coromandel-11.name: Tairua
coromandel-11.bio: A small town at the mouth of the Tairua River and a summer holiday spot on the Coromandel circuit.

coromandel-12.name: Whangamatā
coromandel-12.bio: A beachside town counted among the country's top surf locations, with beach breaks and a bar break.

coromandel-13.name: Buffalo Beach
coromandel-13.bio: A 3 km sandy swimming beach beside Whitianga, named after HMS Buffalo, wrecked there in 1840.
notes: No Wikipedia article of its own; needs a WIKI_IMAGE_OVERRIDES entry.

coromandel-14.name: Cooks Beach
coromandel-14.bio: A 3 km white-sand swimming beach across Mercury Bay from Whitianga, with a lookout at Shakespeare Cliff.
notes: Coordinates moved to the town point per research.

coromandel-15.name: Paku
coromandel-15.bio: A volcanic peak and former pā site above Tairua, climbed for views of the harbour, Pacific and Coromandel Ranges.
notes: Walk length/time not sourced; 1-2 hr visit is an estimate.

coromandel-16.name: Opoutere Beach
coromandel-16.bio: A 1.4 km return DOC walk to over 5 km of white sand beside Wharekawa Harbour, with nesting dotterels.

coromandel-17.name: The Waterworks
coromandel-17.bio: A family park of 70+ water-powered attractions with swimming holes and a water slide, 7 km from Coromandel town.
coromandel-17.hours: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (6:00 PM in peak season)
notes: Peak vs off-season months not confirmed on the official site; opening days are on its calendar. Adult NZD 28.

coromandel-18.name: Ocean Beach (Tairua)
coromandel-18.bio: A beach on Ocean Beach Road at Tairua, recommended for surfing and sun.
notes: Single counted source (Wikivoyage); marginal draw.

hamilton-5.name: Cambridge
hamilton-5.bio: A tree-lined town on the Waikato River with a very English feel, 24 km southeast of Hamilton.
notes: Bio avoids "heritage buildings" (unsourced).

hamilton-6.name: Hakarimata Summit Track
hamilton-6.bio: A 1,349-step climb to a 374 m summit tower with views to the coast and across the Waikato Basin.

hamilton-7.name: Mount Pirongia
hamilton-7.bio: An extinct volcano rising to 959 m, climbed on an advanced DOC track with views to Taranaki and Ruapehu.

hamilton-8.name: Maungatautari
hamilton-8.bio: New Zealand's largest pest-proof fenced eco-sanctuary, around an extinct volcano, promoting kaka and takahe.
notes: Day pass "from NZD 34" (adult); guided tours NZD 50-72. Coordinates at the visitor centre (summit is 4 km north). Closed 25 Dec.

hamilton-9.name: Te Awamutu
hamilton-9.bio: A Waipa District town called the Rose Town of New Zealand, with a museum holding the carved post Te Uenuku.
notes: Museum hours are from Wikivoyage only, so not stated in the bio.

raglan-5.name: Whale Bay
raglan-5.bio: A surf bay 1.5 km west of Manu Bay on the Raglan coast, reached over rocks from its eastern end.
notes: Access across rocks and private land from a travel-guide page only; check with DOC/council.

waitomo-6.name: Te Kuiti Sheep Shearing Statue
waitomo-6.bio: A seven-metre statue of a shearer in Te Kuiti, the Shearing Capital of the World.
notes: World's largest shearer claim is from the Te Kuiti Wikipedia article, hence "Shearing Capital" wording only.

waitomo-7.name: The Big Apple
waitomo-7.bio: A 7.5 m apple statue on State Highway 3 near Hangatiki, with a cafe, on the way to Waitomo.
notes: Cafe hours and whether it still trades are unverified (latest source 2015), so hours are a qualifier and the bio says only "with a cafe". Placement coordinates were the neighbouring Huhu Cafe; used OSM artwork point.

taupo-7.name: Lake Taupō
taupo-7.bio: A crater lake in the caldera of Taupō Volcano and the largest in New Zealand, for cruising, fishing and sailing.

tongariro-7.name: Turangi
tongariro-7.bio: A trout-fishing town at the south end of Lake Taupō, with the 15 km Tongariro River Trail from town.
notes: Category kept as historic per placement.

tongariro-8.name: Tongariro National Trout Centre
tongariro-8.bio: A charitable-trust trout hatchery with a museum, freshwater aquarium and underwater viewing chamber.
notes: Charitable trust, not DOC-run and not free: adult NZD 22. Closed Mondays in winter per a Taupo listing, not the official site, so closedDays omitted.

port-waikato.name: Port Waikato
port-waikato.bio: A surf and whitebaiting town where the Waikato River meets the Tasman Sea, with a surf beach and dunes.
notes: No visitor-guide source beyond Wikipedia; no ticketUrl.

te-aroha.name: Te Aroha
te-aroha.bio: A town below Mount Te Aroha with the country's most intact Edwardian spa and a soda-water geyser.
notes: Pinned at the Mokena Geyser. Spa prices/hours third-party only; spa operator link deliberately not used.

mount-te-aroha.name: Mount Te Aroha
mount-te-aroha.bio: A steep DOC track from Te Aroha Domain to the 952 m top of the Kaimai Range, with 360-degree views.
notes: Return time 5-7 hr from DOC 3 hr one way. Summit point.

hauraki-rail-trail.name: Hauraki Rail Trail
hauraki-rail-trail.bio: A cycle trail of about 160 km, one of the Great Rides, passing Paeroa and the Karangahake Gorge tunnel.
notes: Length: operator says about 160 km, Wikipedia 197 km; bio uses the operator figure.

timber-trail.name: Timber Trail
timber-trail.bio: An 85 km, 2-3 day cycle and walking trail through Pureora Forest Park on old bush tramways, with 35 bridges.
notes: Huts/campsites are paid separately; visit 6-24 hr (2-3 days).

tirau-giant-dog-and-sheep.name: Tirau Giant Dog and Sheep
tirau-giant-dog-and-sheep.bio: A corrugated-iron information centre shaped like a giant dog, beside a building shaped like a sheep.
notes: i-SITE opening hours not checked; exterior viewable any time.

coromandel-1.notes: wiki redirects to the Whanganui A Hei (Cathedral Cove) Marine Reserve article, not the arch; leave wiki and rely on the photo override.

waitomo-4.notes: Remove wiki: it only redirects to Marokopa River.

notes: Held for a photo (applied once one is found): The Waterworks, Ocean Beach (Tairua), Maungatautari, Te Awamutu, Tongariro National Trout Centre, Mount Te Aroha, Timber Trail, Tirau Giant Dog and Sheep.
